value.text:
Wuchang State Superior Normal Institute (國立武昌高等師範學校), also known as 国立武昌高师, was a national teacher-training institution in Wuchang during the Republic of China. It was established in 1913 at the former foreign-language school site in Dongchangkou, using that school’s teaching staff, books and equipment. Formal teaching began on 2 November 1913, when its first intake comprised 124 preparatory students. Its original course structure provided one preparatory year followed by three years of undergraduate study.

In June 1923, the institution’s deliberative council and directors decided to rename it National Wuchang Normal University; education ministry approval followed in February 1924. A further ministry-directed change in September 1924 gave it the name National Wuchang University. In the winter of 1926, that institution and other higher schools, including Hubei Provincial Medical University, merged to establish National Wuchang Sun Yat-sen University.

The school’s academic organization changed over its history. In 1922, four divisions were reorganized into eight departments covering Chinese, history and sociology, education and philosophy, English, mathematics, physics and chemistry, biology, and geography. Reforms described for that period included coeducation, an auditing-student system and replacement of the academic-year system by a credit system. Its motto, adopted in 1919, was 朴、诚、勇.
